steps.title: Rule presence is not a passing result

blocks.text: A Config managed rule evaluates supported resource configuration against its criteria and configured parameters. Its presence is setup evidence, not proof that every resource passed.
Choose the supplied rule, resource scope and parameters. Run or inspect its evaluation, comparing compliant and noncompliant samples. Read each resource ID and compliance result.

steps.title: Check both sides of the boundary

blocks.text: For the supplied rule, compare the approved scope and parameters with the requirement, then inspect both sample evaluations. Tie each resource ID and compliance result to the rule criteria. The acceptable sample should pass; the prohibited sample should be flagged. A sample outside the configured scope cannot validate the intended in-scope criterion.

If the prohibited sample is reported as compliant, inspect scope and parameters against the supplied requirement rather than accepting rule presence as success. Individual results matter. This detection check does not install remediation, and a compliance report does not establish malicious activity.

steps.title: Check the individual evidence
steps.lede: Read the supplied evidence and choose the interpretation that matches the approved settings and individual results.

individual.message: Each conclusion is tied to an individual resource ID and compliance result.

presence.message: Rule presence is setup evidence, not each resource’s compliance result. One supplied row is noncompliant.

all_fail.message: Read individual resource IDs and results. The compliant sample still has its own passing result.

correct.message: You used both individual results, not just rule presence.

incorrect.message: Tie each conclusion to its own evaluation row.

steps.title: Review the configuration evidence
steps.lede: Read the supplied excerpts in this step and decide which correctly select the rule, scope and parameters and verify the individual sample results.

public.prompt:
Read each proposed Config review excerpt and decide whether it meets ALL supplied criteria. Required settings:
```json
{
  "selected_rule": "supplied Config managed rule",
  "resource_scope": "approved sandbox resource scope",
  "parameters": "supplied approved parameters"
}
```
Required sample evidence:
```json
[
  {
    "resource_id": "sample-acceptable",
    "selected_rule": "supplied Config managed rule",
    "resource_scope": "approved sandbox resource scope",
    "parameters": "supplied approved parameters",
    "sample_configuration": "supplied compliant sample",
    "compliance_result": "COMPLIANT"
  },
  {
    "resource_id": "sample-prohibited",
    "selected_rule": "supplied Config managed rule",
    "resource_scope": "approved sandbox resource scope",
    "parameters": "supplied approved parameters",
    "sample_configuration": "supplied noncompliant sample",
    "compliance_result": "NON_COMPLIANT"
  }
]
```
Both samples are in the approved scope. A valid review matches the rule, scope and parameters, retains each resource ID and its expected compliance result, does not accept rule presence alone, and performs no remediation.

review1.message: The rule, scope and parameters match, both resource IDs and their expected results are retained, and no remediation is performed.

review2.message: The supplied prohibited sample must be flagged. Reporting both samples as compliant fails the boundary check; inspect scope and parameters.

review3.message: Rule presence alone omits both individual evaluations and cannot prove compliance.

review4.message: The scope excludes a required sample, so its result cannot validate the intended in-scope criterion.

correct.message: You checked settings, both sample results and the evidence boundary.

incorrect.message: A complete review needs matching settings and both expected individual evaluations, without remediation.

hints: Check the selected scope before trusting a sample result.
Look for both resource IDs, not merely a rule name.
